analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, examining the potential for severe invasive disease caused by Pasteurella multocida following cat bites, particularly in immunocompetent individuals. The central question is whether P. multocida can lead to fatal sepsis in such cases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report and literature review. It includes a single case study of a 51-year-old woman who developed fatal P. multocida sepsis after cat bites, with no known comorbidities. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates, but rather on the case and related literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The case demonstrates that Pasteurella multocida can cause fulminant, fatal sepsis in immunocompetent individuals, challenging the assumption that severe disease is limited to immunocompromised hosts. This highlights the importance of considering P. multocida as a potential pathogen in severe infections following cat bites.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to a single case report, which may not be representative of broader trends. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clinicians should consider initiating empirical treatment early for high-risk cat bites and integrate molecular diagnostics in cases where conventional cultures are negative. Further research is needed to better understand the pathogenic potential of P. multocida in immunocompetent individuals and to refine diagnostic and treatment protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This case report and literature review describe a fatal case of Pasteurella multocida sepsis in a woman without known comorbidities following cat bites. The case challenges the notion that severe P. multocida infections are limited to immunocompromised hosts, emphasizing the need for early antibiotic treatment and the use of molecular diagnostics in culture-negative, life-threatening infections. The review highlights the importance of adhering to current prophylactic guidelines for high-risk cat bites and underscores the necessity for further research to clarify the pathogenic potential of P. multocida in immunocompetent individuals.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是病例报告和文献综述。其中包括一名 51 岁女性的单一案例研究,她在被猫咬伤后患上致命的多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症,且没有已知的合并症。该综述不报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是报告案例和相关文献。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性、致命性脓毒症,挑战了严重疾病仅限于免疫功能低下的 宿主 的假设。这凸显了将多杀性巴氏杆菌视为猫咬伤后严重感染的潜在病原体的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这可能无法代表更广泛的趋势。缺乏关于免疫功能正常个体中多杀性巴氏杆菌感染的频率和严重程度的全面数据,并且分子诊断在早期检测中的作用仍未得到充分探索。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床医生应考虑尽早针对高风险猫咬伤启动经验性 治疗,并在传统培养结果呈阴性的情况下整合分子诊断。需要进一步的研究来更好地了解多杀性巴氏杆菌在免疫功能正常的个体中的致病潜力,并完善诊断和 治疗 方案。

source_body_en: Pasteurella multocida is a common feline oral commensal that typically causes mild local infections after cat bites, but severe invasive disease is rare and predominantly reported in immunocompromised hosts. We report a fatal case of fulminant P. multocida sepsis in a 51-year-old woman without known comorbidities following cat bites. She presented with progressive bilateral upper limb swelling, and then received rabies and tetanus immunoprophylaxis at a local clinic, but rapidly developed septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). Conventional cultures were negative, while metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of wound fluid identified P. multocida on hospital day 3. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy, she died on hospital day 4. This case demonstrates that P. multocida can cause fulminant, fatal sepsis in immunocompetent individuals. It underscores the need for strict adherence to current prophylactic antibiotic guidelines for high-risk cat bites and earlier integration of molecular diagnostics in culture-negative, life-threatening infections. Clinicians should start empirical treatment early and monitor closely when the therapeutic window is short.
abstract_zh: 多杀性巴氏杆菌是一种常见的猫科动物口腔共生菌,通常在猫咬伤后引起轻度局部感染,但严重的侵袭性疾病很少见,主要见于免疫功能低下的 宿主。我们报告了一例暴发性多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症致死病例,患者为一名 51 岁女性,在被猫咬伤后没有已知的合并症。她出现进行性双侧上肢肿胀,随后在当地诊所接受了 狂犬病 和破伤风免疫预防治疗,但很快出现感染性休克、弥散性血管内凝血 (DIC) 和多器官功能障碍综合征 (MODS)。传统培养结果呈阴性,而在住院第 3 天,伤口液体宏基因组下一代测序 (mNGS) 鉴定出多杀性巴氏杆菌。尽管使用了广谱抗生素、机械通气、血管加压药和持续肾脏替代治疗,她还是在住院第 4 天死亡。该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性致命性败血症。它强调需要严格遵守当前针对高风险猫咬伤的预防性抗生素指南,并尽早将分子诊断纳入培养阴性、危及生命的感染中。临床医生应尽早开始经验性 治疗,并在治疗窗口较短时密切监测。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,检查猫咬伤后多杀性巴氏杆菌引起严重侵袭性疾病的可能性,特别是在免疫功能正常的个体中。核心问题是在这种情况下,多杀性巴氏杆菌是否会导致致命的败血症。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是病例报告和文献综述。其中包括一名 51 岁女性的单一案例研究,她在被猫咬伤后患上致命的多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症,且没有已知的合并症。该综述不报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是报告案例和相关文献。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性、致命性脓毒症,挑战了严重疾病仅限于免疫功能低下的 宿主 的假设。这凸显了将多杀性巴氏杆菌视为猫咬伤后严重感染的潜在病原体的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这可能无法代表更广泛的趋势。缺乏关于免疫功能正常个体中多杀性巴氏杆菌感染的频率和严重程度的全面数据,并且分子诊断在早期检测中的作用仍未得到充分探索。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床医生应考虑尽早针对高风险猫咬伤启动经验性 治疗,并在传统培养结果呈阴性的情况下整合分子诊断。需要进一步的研究来更好地了解多杀性巴氏杆菌在免疫功能正常的个体中的致病潜力,并完善诊断和 治疗 方案。

title: Histopathology results of vaccination sites collected from New Zealand white rabbits vaccinated with a lanolin-based Rabisin® vaccine
abstract: This study aimed to assess whether a slow-release water in-oil emulsion rabies vaccine could potentially provide a safe and effective method to improve canine rabies control in future. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of a single dose of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine used in canines (Rabisin®), compared to two doses of Rabisin® in 16 New Zealand white rabbits. Histopathology evaluation of the injection sites revealed only mild microscopic signs of inflammation, no abscessation or granuloma formation in either the lanolin or Rabisin® groups. Six of the eight samples collected from the Rabisin® group demonstrated a mild inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of eosinophils with fewer lymphocytes and scant plasma cells, whereas the remaining two samples showed minimal to no inflammatory changes. The biopsy sample collected on day 89 of the study from a female in the Rabisin® group was found to be within normal limits (no microscopic lesions), while one sample (from male number 21) had a single focus of locally extensive fibrous connective tissue with scant eosinophils and a few lymphocytes and plasma cells within the superficial dermis. The lanolin group had three of the eight samples with a microscopic appearance similar to the majority of the Rabisin® group, while two of the eight samples showed minimal to no inflammatory changes and two other samples showed only scattered, scant eosinophils within the superficial dermis. One of the eight samples collected from the lanolin group was similar to the findings of six of the eight samples collected from the Rabisin® group but had comparatively fewer lymphocytes and plasma cells. No residual mineral oil droplets were found in the lanolin group samples.

analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated the safety and efficacy of a single dose of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine used in canines (Rabisin®), compared to two doses of Rabisin® in 16 New Zealand white rabbits.
analysis.methods: Histopathology evaluation of the injection sites revealed only mild microscopic signs of inflammation, no abscessation or granuloma formation in either the lanolin or Rabisin® groups.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the lanolin-based adjuvant may be a viable alternative to traditional rabies vaccine formulations in terms of minimizing local inflammatory responses.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine (Rabisin®) in New Zealand white rabbits, comparing it to two doses of Rabisin®. Histopathology of injection sites showed mild inflammation in most samples from the Rabisin® group, with some exhibiting minimal to no changes. The lanolin group had similar findings but with fewer inflammatory cells in one sample. These results suggest that the lanolin-based adjuvant may offer a safer alternative for rabies vaccination, though the small sample size and use of rabbits as a model limit the strength of the evidence. The study contributes to understanding vaccine safety in animal models, which could inform future canine rabies control strategies.
